fixtures.rationale: A missing customer name is silently replaced with an empty string and interpolated straight into the greeting, so the caller can no longer tell the name was absent.
A missing line item amount is replaced with zero and folded into the running total, so a missing amount is indistinguishable from a genuine zero charge.
A missing owner is replaced with the placeholder string 'unknown' before being persisted, baking a fabricated value into the stored record.

A null items column means the line items were never recorded, but defaulting to an empty array reports zero chargeable lines as if that were known, so the caller bills nothing instead of learning the order is incomplete.
A missing order id is replaced with the placeholder 'N/A' and written into the report line as though it were a real identifier.
When the date fails to parse, the function fabricates the current instant instead of the event's real date, and the caller has no way to tell parsing failed.
The page size is a setting callers may omit by contract, and 20 is the documented behaviour of omitting it rather than a stand-in for a missing value.
An omittable options bag with a defaulted timeout is standard call-configuration, not a stand-in for a domain value the caller failed to supply.
A retry count is a documented setting callers may omit; defaulting it to 3 is the contract's stated behaviour, not a fabricated domain value.
An optional collaborator falling back to a no-op implementation is the documented behaviour of omitting it, not a fabricated stand-in for missing data.
The output format is a formatting choice the caller may omit, and 'iso' is the documented default rather than a stand-in for a missing value.
A cache miss is converted to an explicit null the caller must check, rather than being replaced with a fabricated customer.
The defaulted empty string is used only to detect absence and immediately turned into an explicit ok: false result, never treated as a real amount.
A missing required environment variable fails fast with a thrown error; the defaulted empty string is only a sentinel used to detect the absence.
A stored null is normalized to undefined, keeping the absence visible for the caller to check instead of substituting a fabricated email.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
